messages:
maya: Heads-up — ~09:40 UTC we saw a 3x tail latency bump on ingress for hosted API. graphs: https://grafana.company/reports/ingress-tail :warning:

sam: saw the alert. grabbing pprof and tcpdump from gateway host-03. suspect tokenization or many small HTTP/2 frames.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout inference:v2.14 -> 10% at 09:38 UTC.

frank: quick flame from host-03: token_split (tokenizer.cpp) 34.8% CPU, writev_syscall 12.5%, http2_frame_send 9.1% — lots of short syscalls.

olivia: kvcache metrics: hit_rate=0.88 (stable), evict/sec spiked 2 -> 60 around 09:39. bursty short requests looks likely.

sam: tcpdump shows many tiny DATA frames (~100-300B) and repeated SETTINGS/PING. grpc write coalescing seems ineffective (small writes).

derek: fwiw I merged a batcher heuristic tweak yesterday (PR #1229) that reduces batch wait for short sequences — could increase fragmentation.

maya: timeline matches PR merge -> canary -> spike. looks suspicious.

frank: also seeing kvcache prefix mismatch: new serialization path emits `meta_v2` keys for some requests while old path still `meta_v1`. that ups misses.

olivia: reproduction idea: hammer gateway with 2-6 token prompts to simulate chat pings and capture per-request write counts. sample curl loop:
```
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do \
  curl -sS -X POST https://gateway/api/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":2}' >/dev/null; \
done
```

sam: short-term mitigation: revert the batcher tweak on canary, enable writev coalescing in proxy, and add short-request sampler to kvcache telemetry.

maya: initiating canary rollback now — will update with latency numbers.

deploy-bot: Rollback of canary inference:v2.14 initiated at 09:50 UTC.

maya: after rollback tail latency returned to baseline within ~30s. strong signal the heuristic change is primary culprit.

derek: ack. I'll open PR to make the small-batch heuristic opt-in and add telemetry counters: `small_batch_hits`, `coalesce_writev_calls`, `kvcache_key_version`. also add an e2e that simulates many very-short requests.

frank: ops notes: when investigating, capture perf + strace on the runtime worker to correlate writev args. example capture:
```
sudo perf record -g -p <pid> -o out.data -- sleep 10
perf script > flame.out
sudo strace -p <pid> -e writev -c -o strace.out
```

olivia: please also add Console spans for ingress: tokenization.ms, parse.ms, writev.calls so we can alert on sudden shifts.

maya: thanks — I'll draft a short postmortem and link the rollback PRs + follow-ups. :thumbsup:
